ety.text: Apocopic form of vibration, vibrator, etc.

senses.d: An atmosphere or aura felt to belong to a person, place or thing.
ex: The couple canceled their night out when they got a bad vibe from the new babysitter.
And I'm here to prove to you / That we can party on the positive side / And pump positive vibes / So come along for the ride

senses.d: Gut feeling, an impression based on intuition instead of solid data.
ex: Analysts trot out all sorts of valuation models, but most of the time, they make educated guesses based on vibes and their gut feeling.
But when decision time came, performance metrics won out over vibes. HH [ChatGPT version] was released on Friday, April 25.

senses.d: The use of AI to perform a task without expertise, generally without validating the output deeply.
ex: So “vibe cooking” does not mean making it up as I go. It means cooking with enough guidance to stay flexible.

senses.d: Something that is good, trendy, pleasant, or atmospheric; a thing or person with a good vibe.
A vibraphone.
Vibration.
A vibrator (sex toy).
ex: […] a vibe that has a separate control unit connected by a thin cable.

senses.d: To stimulate with a vibrator.
To relax and enjoy oneself.
To agree.
ex: Besides, even if you don't vibe with his subject matter, he is a style king of West Coast, down-tempo gangsta-pimp music.
Maria took him through the events of the next morning and his recollection vibed with his statement at the time.

senses.d: To get along; to hit it off.
ex: Sam started out being someone I totally vibed with on every level.
Nervous and shaky but feigning confidence, I completed the interview with ease and even managed to vibe with the country cutie.

senses.d: To feel in agreement with; to appreciate or enjoy.
ex: Nia was glad she'd let Rico bring her to the club as she vibed with the fusion of Latin sounds and American hip-hop.

senses.d: To treat (a fellow performer) in a condescending or insulting manner, typically during a performance or jam session, to signal to them that they are unsatisfactory.
To vibe code.

grp.label: To agree. To get along; to hit it off. To feel in agreement with; to appreciate.

ety.text: Borrowed from English vibe, apocope of vibration.

es:onda.gl: wave (on the surface of a liquid)

ety.text: Inherited from Old Spanish onda, from Latin unda, from Proto-Indo-European *unt-, nasalized form of Proto-Indo-European *wed-.

es:vibra.gl: vibe (atmosphere or aura of a person or place as communicated to and felt by others)

pt:astral.gl: vibe (the atmosphere of a person or situation)

ety.text: Ancient Greek ἄστρον (ástron)bor. Latin astrum Proto-Indo-European *h₂el- Proto-Indo-European *-is Proto-Indo-European *h₂élisder.? Proto-Italic *-ālis Latin -ālis Late Latin astrālislbor. Portuguese astral Learned borrowing from Late Latin astrālis. By surface analysis, astro + -al.
Latin bacillumbor. Spanish bacilo Spanish -ar Spanish bacilar From bacilo + -ar.
From French vibrant, from Latin vibrans, present participle of vibrare (“to vibrate”). See vibrate.

senses.d: Pulsing with energy or activity.
Lively and vigorous.
Vibrating, resonant or resounding.
ex: A vibrant voice in the true sense is of course desirable

senses.d: Bright.
Any of a class of consonants including taps and trills.

ety.text: From French vibration, from Latin vibrātiō (“a shaking or brandishing”), from vibrō (“shake, vibrate”); see vibrate. Morphologically vibrate + -ion.

senses.d: The act of vibrating or the condition of being vibrated.
ex: You will see a tiny flutter, a shiver, a vibration along the luff. That flutter is your friend.

senses.d: Any periodic process, especially a rapid linear motion of a body about an equilibrium position.
A single complete vibrating motion.
A vibrational energy of spiritual nature through which mediumistic and other paranormal phenomena are conveyed or affected.
An instinctively sensed emotional aura or atmosphere.
ex: I'm pickin' up good vibrations / She's giving me the excitations.

ety.text: From Latin vibrātiōnem, equivalent to vibrar + -ción.
